abstract_sentences.text: Graph clustering is a fundamental task in data analysis, aiming at grouping nodes with similar characteristics in the graph into clusters.

evidence.anchor: Graph clustering is a fundamental task

abstract_sentences.text: This problem has been widely explored using graph neural networks (GNNs) due to their ability to leverage node attributes and graph topology for effective cluster assignments.
abstract_sentences.bridge: moves from task to the technical context

evidence.anchor: widely explored using graph neural networks

abstract_sentences.text: However, representations learned through GNNs typically struggle to capture global relationships between nodes via local message-passing mechanisms.
abstract_sentences.bridge: first gap after the GNN premise

abstract_sentences.text: Moreover, the redundancy and noise inherently present in graph data may easily result in node representations lacking compactness and robustness.
To address these issues, we propose a conjoint framework CoCo, which captures compactness and consistency in the learned node representations for deep graph clustering.

evidence.anchor: we propose a conjoint framework CoCo

abstract_sentences.text: Technically, our CoCo leverages graph convolutional filters to learn robust node representations from both local and global views, and then encodes them into low-rank compact embeddings, thus effectively removing the redundancy and noise as well as uncovering the intrinsic underlying structure.
To further enrich the node semantics, we develop a consistency learning strategy based on compact embeddings to facilitate knowledge transfer from the two perspectives.
Our experimental results indicate that our CoCo outperforms state-of-the-art counterparts on various datasets.
abstract_sentences.bridge: places the empirical claim after the method

abstract_sentences.text: The code is available at https://github.com/juweipku/CoCo.
abstract_sentences.function_encoding_note: The closed schema has no reproducibility/availability function; impact_claim is used for this code-availability sentence.

formal_objects.input: Attribute graph G={V,E,X,A}; Algorithm 1 also requires cluster number C.
formal_objects.output: Fused ZF followed by K-means clustering result c.
formal_objects.states: X̃l/X̃g, Zl/Zg, concatenated Z, shared subspace Λ, posterior γ, reconstruction Ẑ, residual compact states Z̃l/Z̃g, distributions pi/qi, ZF.
formal_objects.assumptions: Personalized PageRank diffusion with α∈(0,1); sparsification/symmetrization; K≪D; equal GMM priors; isotropic covariance; EM result is injected outside gradient flow through Eq. 5.

component_problem_map.addresses: local message passing misses long-range relations and deepening causes over-smoothing

component_problem_map.component: shared low-rank GMM subspace and reconstruction
component_problem_map.addresses: redundancy/noise and semantic gap between views
EM is outside gradient flow and a pure low-rank constraint may over-smooth or collapse

algorithm.input_output: Input G and C; output c.
algorithm.key_invariants_or_state_relations: The same Λ̂ is updated for the concatenated two-view embedding; each outer iteration updates pi/qi and minimizes the symmetric KL.
algorithm.complexity_statement: Appendix E gives per-epoch O(NDK+NMD) time and O(ND+NM) space after sparse-diffusion preprocessing.

equation_theory_inventory.label: Anchor similarity distributions p_i and q_i

results.name: Theorem 1
results.assumptions: Normalized Laplacians for local/global views and generalized smoothing filter with positive k values.
results.conclusion: Set each k to the corresponding maximal Laplacian eigenvalue to pursue a low-pass filter.
results.empirical_correspondence: Figure 7 compares GCF+MLP and GCN across layers, not choices of k.

evidence.anchor: optimal choice to pursue low-pass filters

results.name: Remark 1
results.assumptions: The M-step increases Q and the H inequality follows from Jensen's inequality.
results.conclusion: The EM likelihood is non-decreasing per iteration.
results.empirical_correspondence: Table 6 reports NMI and runtime shares, not a likelihood trace.

results.name: Theorem 2
results.assumptions: Converged subspace training, Eq. 4 reconstruction, and posterior weights summing to one.
results.conclusion: Claims individual mass conservation and maximal variation preservation for the reconstruction.
results.empirical_correspondence: Figure 2 and noisy BAT Table 3 are component/performance checks, not direct mass or variation measurements.

final_judgment.single_storyline: CoCo turns two diagnosed GNN clustering gaps into one chain: local/global views, shared low-rank compactness, then relational consistency, followed by fused K-means clustering.
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: The main body keeps the problem framing, Figure 1, Eq. 1–7, primary results, selected component/loss/sensitivity checks, noise/graph-type/efficiency/transfer results, and conclusion.
final_judgment.appendix_moves: The appendix moves proofs, generic EM derivation, Algorithm 1, complexity derivation, implementation configuration, extended baselines/loss/sensitivity/GCF results, and related work.
final_judgment.best_pattern: A single overview diagram is followed by view extraction → compactness → consistency, then experiments ordered as full result → component/loss checks → applicability and cost.
final_judgment.largest_gap: Mechanism claims about direct redundancy/noise removal and long-range capture are supported mainly by final performance, noisy-graph results, and qualitative plots; they lack direct intermediate mechanism measurements. Table 1 gains and the universal Table 7 statement also have internal conflicts.
final_judgment.transfer_rule: For a multi-component method, bind each component to a legible representation transform or loss, then close the narrative with a full-model result, a component deletion, and a nearest-surrogate comparison.
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: This rule applies when components can be independently deleted or substituted; coupled components sharing an inseparable optimization state require direct measurements or purpose-built counterfactuals.
